h34s brings Scala.js handlers to Nuxt/Nitro with a primary ZIO API and a first-class Kyo API. Each uses its own effect runtime. Application modules own models, services, configuration, and the `AppHandler` that resolves handler dependencies.

These notes are attached to the GitHub prerelease only after the release workflow publishes the artifacts and verifies authenticated consumers against GitHub Packages.

## Install

Artifacts use organization **`dev.yuri4n`**, version **`0.1.0-alpha.1`**, and the private Maven registry at `https://maven.pkg.github.com/yuri4n/h34s`. Use sbt's `%%%` operator for the `_sjs1_3` coordinates.

Follow the [installation and authentication guide](https://github.com/yuri4n/h34s/blob/release/0.1.0-alpha.1/docs/releases.md). Downloads require repository access and a classic GitHub token with `read:packages`. The h34s repository's own workflows can use their `GITHUB_TOKEN`; other repositories, including `yurian.land`, must supply a classic PAT through Actions secrets because Maven packages use repository-scoped permissions. Install npm **`h3@1.15.4`** in the Nuxt application as well.

| Artifact | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `h3-ext` | Native h3 bindings and transport types |
| `zio-h3-ext` | ZIO handlers, request context, errors, and streaming |
| `kyo-h3-ext` | Kyo handlers and request cleanup |
| `zio-js-ext` | ZIO helpers for JavaScript interoperation |
| `native-converter-zio-ext` | Native conversion for ZIO data types |
| `native-converter-zio-json-ext` | Native conversion for ZIO JSON values |
| `native-converter-zio-schema-ext` | Optional ZIO Schema/native-value conversion |
| `zio-h3-schema-ext` | Optional schema-based ZIO request decoding |
| `nuxthub-ext` | Native NuxtHub KV contract |
| `zio-nuxthub-ext` | Optional ZIO KV adapter |
| `kyo-nuxthub-ext` | Optional Kyo KV adapter |

Native bindings have no effect runtime dependency. ZIO consumers do not acquire Kyo, Kyo consumers do not acquire ZIO, and schema support stays optional. Applications, examples, aggregates, and the experimental migration module are excluded from library publication.

## Features and behavior

- `ZHandler.define` and `KHandler.define` hide native conversion and effect execution. Application-owned `AppHandler` modules provide ordinary ZIO environments/layers or Kyo `Env` services.
- Approved safe errors retain their messages and status. Unexpected failures return `500` with `Internal server error` outside development. Nuxt's server-owned development flag enables causes and traces; Scala.js source maps locate original Scala code during development.
- The ZIO API supports scoped streams over direct Node HTTP. Kyo handlers own request cleanup and preserve rejected request-body Promises in the typed error channel.
- `readBodyWithSchema` lets ZIO applications put transformations and validation on their models. The optional native schema codec uses explicit converter ownership. ZIO JSON numbers convert through JavaScript Double precision without an intermediate Float narrowing.
- NuxtHub 0.10.8 KV adapters expose native `get`, `set`, `has`, `delete`, and `keys` operations through ZIO or Kyo. Applications supply the configured KV object; the libraries do not import an application's generated `@nuxthub/kv` module.
- Development loads linked Scala.js modules directly and reloads Nitro's worker after linking. `pnpm build` clears previous output and production-links both example applications before Nuxt builds, preventing stale development output from being packaged after a failed link.

Generated h3 facades are included in `h3-ext`; consumers no longer need locally generated Ivy artifacts. Source integrations that imported `typings.h3` or `typings.std` should use `dev.yuri4n.h34s.facades.h3` or `dev.yuri4n.h34s.facades.std`.

## Toolchain and release checks

Use **Scala.js 1.22.0**, **Node 24**, **pnpm 10.34.4**, and **sbt 1.11.7**. Native and ZIO modules use **Scala 3.5.2**. Kyo modules use **Scala 3.9.0** and **Kyo 1.0.0-RC7**, whose macros require **Java 25**. Java 25 builds both APIs; the application runtime is Node.

Release gates cover handler, schema, application, and KV tests; production linking; POM validation; and three independent Maven consumers. The ZIO, Kyo, and optional Schema/JSON consumers collectively resolve all eleven artifacts, compile and link without repository source dependencies, and serve real h3 requests. The workflow repeats the consumer checks against the private registry before creating the prerelease. KV operations are tested separately with the pinned Unstorage memory fixture.

## Alpha limits

- Binary and source jars are included. **Scaladoc jars are omitted** because Scala 3.5's documentation generator fails while reading generated inline h3 facades. Use the [guides](https://github.com/yuri4n/h34s/tree/v0.1.0-alpha.1/docs) and source jars.
- Kyo streaming, Kyo Schema, schema-backed JSON/YAML codecs, automatic route discovery, and Scala-to-TypeScript wire generation remain pending. The optional ZIO Schema codec supports a bounded set of shapes; see its [supported forms](https://github.com/yuri4n/h34s/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.1/docs/schema.md#supported-native-schema-forms).
- ZIO streaming targets direct Node HTTP. Nitro's socketless local-fetch path and other deployment adapters need separate lifecycle support. Kyo RC7 logs request finalizer failures rather than changing the handler response.
- NuxtHub support covers KV, not DB/Drizzle, Blob, or deployment resources. TTL depends on the storage driver, and interrupting a waiting effect does not cancel an already-started storage write. See the [KV guide](https://github.com/yuri4n/h34s/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.1/docs/nuxthub.md).
- Application-scoped Skunk pooling, deployable application packaging, Nix/NixOS support, and sbt-native-packager remain separate work. Independent h3 consumer checks do not establish every external Nuxt application or deployment target.
